subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Nudge vs Ban: When to Use What
description: A quick, practical guide to Nudge vs Ban: When to Use What.

hook.text: New York banned large sodas. Courts overturned it. Other cities nudged smaller cups as defaults.

buildup.text: Bans restrict freedom entirely. Nudges preserve it. But nudges are weaker.

discovery.text: For severe harms like lead paint, bans are appropriate. For preference-based behaviors like diet, nudges respect.

twist.text: Sugar taxes are a middle path: they increase cost without banning. But they disproportionately burden low-income.

climax.text: Policy design should match the intervention strength to the harm level. Light nudges for minor harms, strong.

punchline.text: Nudge when you can. Ban when you must. Tax as a last resort.

quiz.question: When is a ban more appropriate than a nudge?
options: Whenever the government disagrees with consumer choices
When the harm is severe and cannot be adequately addressed by preserving choice
Bans are always preferable to nudges
